I still feel like I have plenty of energy to go jogging and manage my shifts at the plant, so I don't think those are issues for me.\n\nDoctor: You mentioned you haven't been keeping track of your menstrual periods, but can you tell me if you've had any menstrual periods at all in the past three months?\n\nPatient: I honestly don't know for sure. I haven't been paying any attention to my cycle lately, so I can't say if I've had one in the last three months.\n\nDoctor: Have you had any menstrual periods at all in the past six months, or has your menstrual cycle stopped completely?\n\nPatient: I honestly can't tell you if it has stopped completely or not. I haven't tracked my cycle at all over the last six months with how busy I've been, so I'm just not sure.\n\nDoctor: Can you confirm whether you have had any menstrual periods at all in the past year, or if your menstrual cycle has stopped completely since you started restricting your food intake and increasing your exercise?\n\nPatient: I honestly don't know, even looking back over the whole year. I've been so focused on my weight and my new role at work that my periods haven't even been on my radar.\n\nDoctor: Can you confirm whether you have had any menstrual periods at all in the past year, and if not, do you think this could be related to your weight loss and restrictive eating habits?\n\nPatient: I honestly can't confirm since I haven't kept track of my periods at all this past year. I also haven't really thought about whether that would have anything to do with my eating or my weight, since it's just not something I've paid attention to.\n\nDoctor: If you were to gain a small amount of weight, do you think your menstrual cycle would return to normal, or do you believe your weight and menstrual cycle are unrelated?\n\nPatient: I'm really not sure about that, as I've never actually thought about whether my weight and my menstrual cycle are connected. It's just not something that has crossed my mind at all.\n\nDoctor: If you were to stop restricting your food intake and return to a normal eating pattern, do you think your menstrual cycle would resume, and is this something you would be willing to try to see if it affects your menstrual cycle?\n\nPatient: I'm really not sure about my cycle, and at my age, I hadn't even connected the two. Honestly, I'm very hesitant to change my eating habits right now because the idea of losing control over my weight makes me so anxious.\n\nDoctor: Can you confirm whether you have had any menstrual periods at all in the past year, and if not, are you willing to consider that your restrictive eating habits and significant weight loss may be contributing to the absence of your menstrual cycle?\n\nPatient: I'm honestly not sure about my cycle, and I haven't really thought about it in relation to my weight. I feel like everyone is overstating how much weight I've lost, whereas I just see myself as being disciplined and staying active.\n\nDoctor: Can you understand that your restrictive eating habits and significant weight loss might be causing your menstrual cycle to stop, and would you be willing to work on changing your eating habits to potentially restore your menstrual cycle?\n\nPatient: I'm really not sure, and with my busy schedule and my age, I haven't really thought about my cycle stopping or focused on it. I still believe my husband and doctor are exaggerating my weight loss and any health risks, as I feel completely healthy and active. Because of that, I'm not really willing to change my eating habits right now.\n\nDoctor: Can you understand that your restrictive eating habits and significant weight loss might be causing your menstrual cycle to stop, and would you be willing to work on changing your eating habits to potentially restore your menstrual cycle, considering the potential long-term health consequences?\n\nPatient: I honestly didn't realize my menstrual cycle could be related to my weight, and it's just not something I've thought about. I feel like these long-term health concerns are being exaggerated because I still feel completely healthy, energetic, and active every day. Because of that, I'm really not ready to change how I eat right now.\n\nDoctor: Do you think your restrictive eating habits and significant weight loss are more closely related to your desire to control your weight and body shape, or to an intense fear of gaining weight or becoming fat?\n\nPatient: Honestly, those two things are completely tied together for me. My self-worth and whether I'm succeeding in life feel entirely dependent on keeping my stomach flat and looking slim in my uniform and dance group. At the same time, if the scale goes up by even half a pound, I feel an intense panic and a complete loss of control, which drives me to restrict my eating even more to make up for it.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe how your fear of gaining weight influences your decision to restrict your food intake and engage in excessive exercise, and do you think you could ever imagine a scenario where you wouldn't be fearful of gaining weight?\n\nPatient: If the scale goes up even half a pound, or if I eat rich foods like roti or macaroni pie, I panic and feel like I've completely lost control, which drives me to immediately restrict my food to just coffee and increase my jogging to make up for it. It's very hard to imagine a scenario where I'm not afraid of gaining weight, because maintaining this strict discipline feels like the only way I can cope with all of life's demands and feel successful right now.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me more about what specifically happens or what you fear will happen if you were to gain a significant amount of weight, and how that fear influences your daily decisions about eating and exercise?\n\nPatient: If I were to gain weight, I feel like I would completely lose control and fail to look the disciplined way I'm supposed to as a supervisor and dancer. This fear makes me strictly limit my food, like telling my family I already ate at work and cutting my dinner portions to almost nothing. It also drives me to jog and do yoga constantly to make sure I maintain a slim, tight appearance.\n\nDoctor: Do you think your fear of gaining weight is more about avoiding a specific weight or body shape, or is it more about achieving a certain ideal of thinness and control over your body?"
  }
